summary: Verified the AdminPortal Delete Employee fix for the no-profile-photo case. Backend: 55/57 passed, 1 skipped, 1 pre-existing failure. Added targeted regression test test_delete_employee_without_photo_file_id which reproduces the exact bug scenario (employee created via POST /api/employees never uploads a photo → DELETE /api/employees/{id} now returns 200 instead of the previous erroneous 404 'Employee not found'). Cascade verified: employee absent from GET /api/employees and login returns 401. Also verified employee role gets 403 on DELETE /api/employees/{id}. Admin missing employee → 404, unauth delete → 401 (all pass). Frontend UI: admin logged in via preview URL, created TEST_NoPhotoUI_682486 (no photo), opened dialog via data-testid=delete-employee-{id}, Cancel closed the dialog and left the employee intact, re-opened and Confirm removed it (toast 'TEST_NoPhotoUI_682486 was removed', no in-dialog error surfaced, employee absent from listing, login returns 401). Root-cause fix in router.remove_employee (project id + None check instead of truthiness on empty projection) is correct and effective.

minor.issue: Returns 404 because seeded employee emp-raj no longer exists in db.employees (removed by previous test/user action). seed.py only re-inserts EMPLOYEES when db.vendors is empty, so employee rows are not restored on restart. This breaks test_admin_employee_activity and any UI depending on seeded emp-raj.

User expected Ananya Shah removed but login with +91 98765 42101 / Welcome@123 currently returns 200. Root cause: seed_database re-creates the emp-ananya USER row on every backend startup even after admin deletes the employee (loop at seed.py L44-47 inserts a user if missing regardless of whether the employee document was deleted). The employee document itself is gone (not in /api/employees) but the login account persists → orphaned user with no employee record. This is a seed idempotency bug independent of the current fix.

action_items: seed.py: after admin deletion, the user-row seeding loop (lines 44-47) re-creates emp-ananya (and any other deleted seed employee) on every backend restart. Either (a) skip user-seed when the corresponding employee doc is missing, or (b) re-seed both employee+user together, or (c) drop the deleted-seed IDs from EMPLOYEES list. Preferred: guard the user-seed loop with an `active` flag / deleted-employees allow-list.
seed.py: consider re-inserting missing seeded employees (emp-raj) when db.employees is empty rather than gating on db.vendors, otherwise seeded employees permanently disappear once deleted.
(Optional) TestAdminFlows.test_admin_employee_activity relies on emp-raj existing; either seed guarantees emp-raj or the test should create its own employee (recommend seed fix, per above).
critical_code_review_comments: router.remove_employee fix is correct: projection now returns {id, photo_file_id} so an employee without photo_file_id still yields a non-None doc; the `if employee is None` check correctly disambiguates missing vs no-photo. Good fix.
Cascade order (employees → users → files soft-delete) is sensible; collections history retained by design.
Seed function seed.py seeds users independently of employees, creating orphaned login accounts after admin deletion — see action_items.
AdminPortal.jsx / EmployeeDeleteDialog.jsx UX solid: loading state, data-testid coverage on dialog + buttons + error, toast on success.

If retesting Ananya removal, note that seed.py re-adds the emp-ananya USER row on backend restart even though the employee document stays deleted (see backend_issues.minor and action_items). rca of the issue: BUG (fixed): remove_employee originally projected only {photo_file_id: 1, _id: 0}. For an employee without a photo, MongoDB returned {} (an empty but non-None dict). The old code likely used `if not employee` which treated {} as falsy → raised 404 'Employee not found' even though the row existed. FIX: projection now includes `id: 1` and the check is `if employee is None`, so an existing employee (with or without photo) always evaluates to a non-None dict and proceeds to deletion. Verified with two backend tests plus one full UI walkthrough on a freshly created no-photo employee.
